    {"id": "K3.1", "basis": "default", "answer": "Assume a Python script accepts one or more positional CSV paths; each UTF-8 CSV has a header with region, product, units, and unit_price columns. Print labeled total revenue, revenue per region, and units per product to stdout. Discovery should check for an existing sales-record schema or naming convention before these defaults are fixed."},
    {"id": "K3.2", "basis": "default", "answer": "Assume exit status 0 on success, 2 for command-line usage errors, and 1 for file or record errors; report errors on stderr without a partial summary."},
    {"id": "K4.1", "basis": "default", "answer": "Assume record revenue is units multiplied by unit_price, totals combine all supplied files, and the process ends after printing the summary. Use exact decimal arithmetic; no currency conversion or rounding policy is assumed."},
    {"id": "K4.2", "basis": "default", "answer": "Assume missing required headers or values, non-integer or negative units, non-finite or negative prices, and unreadable or malformed files are invalid. Discovery should seek evidence of returns or other valid negative records before fixing this rule."},
    {"id": "K5.1", "basis": "default", "answer": "Input files remain owned by the caller; aggregation state lives in the process and ends when it exits. The tool creates no persistent state."},
    {"id": "K5.2", "basis": "default", "answer": "The caller controls access to input files and output streams. Assume files do not change while being read; a restart recomputes from the files available then."},
    {"id": "K6.1", "basis": "inspect", "answer": "Discovery should establish the available Python version and any workspace requirement; absent a requirement, target an available supported Python 3 runtime."},
    {"id": "K6.2", "basis": "default", "answer": "Assume the Python standard library is sufficient; no third-party dependency is required."},
    {"id": "K6.3", "basis": "default", "answer": "Assume configuration consists of the positional input paths; no ports, environment variables, or configuration files are required."},
    {"id": "K7.1", "basis": "default", "answer": "Keep CSV reading and validation, aggregation, and command-line output separable enough to test independently and through the command."},
    {"id": "K8.1", "basis": "default", "answer": "Assume standard-library unittest, runnable with python -m unittest discover; discovery should first check for an applicable workspace test convention."},
    {"id": "K8.2", "basis": "default", "answer": "Run the command against representative temporary CSV files and check stdout, stderr, and exit status; cover all three aggregates, multiple files, and invalid input."},

    {"id": "K11.1", "basis": "default", "answer": "The main rejection risks are assuming the wrong CSV schema or revenue rules and producing incorrect aggregates or unusable errors."},

  "summary": "S1 — Fact: deliver a Python terminal tool in the repository that reads sales CSV files and prints the three requested aggregates; the user can use the changed source checkout after final return, and no deployed target is requested. Open questions: discovery should first inspect the empty repository and available environment, then seek any available team or workspace conventions, channels, internal sites or docs, private repositories, owners, and meanings of sales fields; these are leads, not verified sources. Schema and revenue-rule discovery blocks fixing parsing, validation, and aggregation; runtime discovery blocks fixing Python compatibility. If evidence is absent, the recorded defaults answer those questions. No sensitive locator was supplied; any discovered sensitive locator belongs only in an authorized private store, never in committed KNOWLEDGE/. This is a noninteractive CLI, so actor identification, shared sessions, and hidden interactive state do not apply; the recorded file and process-state defaults govern execution. S2 — Fact: add tests for the requested behavior; discovery should first check the workspace for a test convention, which blocks fixing the test command, with standard-library unittest as the recorded default if no convention exists. The tests and their results become available in the returned source checkout after final return."
